dedupe_keys.name: openclsim open source complex logistics simulation

description: OpenCLSim is a Python package for rule-driven scheduling of cyclic activities, used to compare alternative operating strategies of complex logistics such as marine construction, dredging and waterborne transport of material. Users compose sites and stockpiles, resources (processors and transporters such as vessels) and activities (loading, sailing, unloading and rule-based operations) from reusable mixins on the SimPy discrete-event engine, and every event is logged for analysis. It is developed by the Ports and Waterways group of TU Delft, with a background paper at the World Dredging Congress (WODCON) 2022, notebooks with examples and an online book. It is location independent and works at project, port or regional scale. The package is on PyPI (1.6.3 of 29 September 2025) and GitHub under the MIT licence, free, with a Zenodo DOI for releases; commits continued in October 2025. Caveats: the online documentation still shows version 1.4.2, and realistic use needs project-specific production rates and vessel data. OpenCLSim supports capacity planning and optimisation of waterborne logistics chains and the comparison of operating strategies under disruption for resilience, and complements the OpenTNSim vessel traffic model from the same group, catalogued here.
